page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.4xlarge is an enhanced general-purpose virtual machine configuration built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores via multithreading, driven by a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. The CPU features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations show consistent mid-tier performance across memory operations, recording 845.59 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and 88.26 GB/sec for large-block uncached memory reads. The instance does not bundle local disk storage, requiring external cloud storage volumes for persistent data, and does not include dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs. Networking is provisioned with a 6 Gbps baseline bandwidth capacity.

Benchmarking data reflects balanced computational throughput. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,601 and a PassMark CPU score of 21,105.84. In specialized CPU tests, it produced 15.86 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, decompressed bzip3 data at 84.09 GB/sec across all threads, and sustained static web serving throughput of 21.41 GB/sec. Lightweight AI workloads show solid execution speeds, achieving 271.33 tokens per second on text generation using a small 135M language model.

With dedicated vCPU allocation and a balanced resource profile, ecs.g7se.4xlarge delivers dependable resource density without the overhead of unused accelerator hardware. It is technically suited for multi-tier web applications, Redis caching layers, enterprise backend services, software compilation, and moderate transactional databases requiring persistent block storage attachments.
